english_paragraphs: OK, often said to be the planet's most frequently spoken word, began as a newspaper gag. From 1838 abbreviations were all the vogue in Boston's papers, and the craze turned comic through deliberate misspellings: O.W. for 'oll wright', K.Y. for 'know yuse'. The humour lay in the persona of an uneducated bumpkin.

On 23 March 1839 a Boston Morning Post satire took a swipe at a contemporary, the Providence Journal, over a mock society parodying an ordinance against ringing dinner bells. It carried the first known 'o.k.', glossed as 'all correct'. The letters stood for a knowingly illiterate 'oll korrect'. The presumed writer was the editor, Charles Gordon Greene.

Partisan politics propagated the letters nationwide. In 1840 Martin Van Buren, the incumbent president, sought re-election. His New York backers, punning on his nickname 'Old Kinderhook', after his birthplace, formed the Democratic O.K. Club, making the letters a double-meaning slogan. That November William Henry Harrison unseated him, 234 electoral votes to 60.

On 30 March 1840 the New York Morning Herald printed a fabricated smear: the former president Andrew Jackson, a supposedly inept speller, had marked paperwork O.K., for 'Ole Kurrek'. Jackson spelled reasonably well and never marked documents O.K. Within about twenty years, people did so in earnest. The bogus notation was merely premature.

Rival stories offered exotic pedigrees: Choctaw 'okeh' and Greek 'ola kala'. Authoritative dictionaries favoured Choctaw as late as 1961. In 1963–64 the linguist Allen Walker Read excavated the neglected Boston provenance from archival newspapers in six influential American Speech articles. Most dictionaries now embrace his derivation, a pedigree of bad spelling and dinner-bell satire.
chinese_source_paragraphs: OK，常被说成是全世界**最常**(most frequently)说出的词，起初只是报纸上的一个**噱头**(gag)。从1838年起，**缩写**(abbreviations)**风靡**(all the vogue)于波士顿各大报纸，而且这股**狂热**(craze)也变得**滑稽**(comic)起来，通过**故意的**(deliberate)**错误拼写**(misspellings)：用 O.W. 代表 'oll wright'，用 K.Y. 代表 'know yuse'。**幽默**(humour)**在于**(lay in)一个**没受过教育的**(uneducated)**乡巴佬**(bumpkin)**人物角色**(persona)。

1839年3月23日，《波士顿晨邮报》的一篇**讽刺文章**(satire)**抨击了**(took a swipe at)一个**同时期的**(contemporary)报纸《普罗维登斯日报》，话题是一个**恶搞的**(mock)社团，它**戏仿**(parodying)一项禁止敲开饭铃的**法令**(ordinance)。它刊载了已知最早的“o.k.”，**被注释为**(glossed as)“all correct”（完全正确）。这两个字母代表的是**有意**(knowingly)写成**文盲**(illiterate)拼法的'oll korrect'。**推定的**(presumed)作者是该报纸的**编辑**(editor)查尔斯·戈登·格林。

**党派**(Partisan)政治在全国**宣传了**(propagated)这些字母。1840年，**在任**(incumbent)总统马丁·范布伦寻求**连任**(re-election)。他在纽约的**拥护者**(backers)**拿**(punning on)他的绰号 'Old Kinderhook' **玩双关**(punning on)，这个绰号得名于他的**出生地**(birthplace)，他们成立了民主党 O.K. 俱乐部，让这两个字母成了一句**一语双关的**(double-meaning)**口号**(slogan)。那年11月，威廉·亨利·哈里森**把**(unseated)他**赶下台**(unseated)，**选举人票**(electoral votes)为234张对60张。

1840年3月30日，《纽约先驱晨报》刊登了一则**捏造的**(fabricated)**抹黑**(smear)：前总统安德鲁·杰克逊，一个**据称**(supposedly)拼写**笨拙的**(inept)人，曾在**公文**(paperwork)上标注 O.K.，用以代表“Ole Kurrek”。杰克逊拼写得**还算/尚且**(reasonably)不错，并且从没在文件上批注过 O.K.。在大约二十年内，人们就**认真地**(in earnest)这样做了。这个**伪造的**(bogus)**批注**(notation)，不过是出现**过早**(premature)而已。

与之竞争的说法给出了种种**异域的**(exotic)**来历**(pedigrees)，比如乔克托语的 'okeh'和希腊语的 'ola kala'。**权威**(Authoritative)词典直到1961年还倾向于乔克托语一说。1963至1964年，语言学家艾伦·沃克·里德从**档案**(archival)报纸中**发掘**(excavated)出长期被**忽视的**(neglected)波士顿**起源**(provenance)，这些发现发表在《美国语言》杂志的六篇**影响深远的**(influential)文章里。如今大多数词典都**采纳了**(embrace)他的**词源**(derivation)解释，那是一段由错误拼写和开饭铃讽刺文构成的来历。

sentences.english: Jackson spelled reasonably well and never marked documents O.K.
sentences.chinese_source: 杰克逊拼写得**还算/尚且**(reasonably)不错，并且从没在文件上批注过 O.K.。

sentences.english: Within about twenty years, people did so in earnest.
sentences.chinese_source: 在大约二十年内，人们就**认真地**(in earnest)这样做了。

sentences.english: The bogus notation was merely premature.
sentences.chinese_source: 这个**伪造的**(bogus)**批注**(notation)，不过是出现**过早**(premature)而已。

sentences.english: Rival stories offered exotic pedigrees: Choctaw 'okeh' and Greek 'ola kala'.
sentences.chinese_source: 与之竞争的说法给出了种种**异域的**(exotic)**来历**(pedigrees)，比如乔克托语的 'okeh'和希腊语的 'ola kala'。

sentences.english: Authoritative dictionaries favoured Choctaw as late as 1961.
sentences.chinese_source: **权威**(Authoritative)词典直到1961年还倾向于乔克托语一说。

sentences.english: In 1963–64 the linguist Allen Walker Read excavated the neglected Boston provenance from archival newspapers in six influential American Speech articles.
sentences.chinese_source: 1963至1964年，语言学家艾伦·沃克·里德从**档案**(archival)报纸中**发掘**(excavated)出长期被**忽视的**(neglected)波士顿**起源**(provenance)，这些发现发表在《美国语言》杂志的六篇**影响深远的**(influential)文章里。

sentences.english: Most dictionaries now embrace his derivation, a pedigree of bad spelling and dinner-bell satire.
sentences.chinese_source: 如今大多数词典都**采纳了**(embrace)他的**词源**(derivation)解释，那是一段由错误拼写和开饭铃讽刺文构成的来历。

approved_summary: 1838年起，波士顿报纸流行故意拼错词再缩写；1839年出现已知最早的“o.k.”。
o.k.取自all correct的故意错拼oll korrect，意为“完全正确”，笑点在模仿文盲口吻。
1840年，范布伦阵营以绰号Old Kinderhook的缩写OK，兼指他本人和“完全正确”，用作竞选口号。
范布伦败选，OK仍流传；杰克逊用它批文件的传闻是捏造，但约二十年内人们已认真如此批注。
语言学家里德于1963至1964年查旧报，重建波士顿词源；多数词典采纳，取代早先乔克托语等说法。
